blocks.prompt: 2 (i) Evaluate \((1+\omega-\omega^{2})^{8}\). [The book prints \((1+\omega-\omega)^{8}\); see the book correction below.]
blocks.explanation: An evaluation with \(\omega\): we must reduce the expression to a simple number using only \(\omega^{3}=1\) and \(1+\omega+\omega^{2}=0\). Plan: first turn each bracket into a single term (or recognise it as \(\omega\) or \(\omega^{2}\)), then raise to the power, then reduce the powers of \(\omega\) by dividing by 3. Expanding an 8th power directly would be very long, so simplifying the bracket first is the key.
steps:
Step 1: Simplify the bracket
\[1+\omega-\omega^{2}=(1+\omega)-\omega^{2}\]
\[=-\omega^{2}-\omega^{2}\]
\[=-2\omega^{2}\]
Why: From \(1+\omega+\omega^{2}=0\) we get \(1+\omega=-\omega^{2}\); then add the like terms.

Step 2: Raise to the power 8
\[(-2\omega^{2})^{8}=(-2)^{8}(\omega^{2})^{8}\]
\[=256\,\omega^{16}\]
Why: Power of a product: \((ab)^{n}=a^{n}b^{n}\). An even power of a negative number is positive: \((-2)^{8}=256\); and \((\omega^{2})^{8}=\omega^{16}\).

Step 3: Reduce the power of omega
\[\omega^{16}=(\omega^{3})^{5}\cdot\omega\]
\[\omega^{16}=\omega\]
Why: \(16=3\times5+1\), and \((\omega^{3})^{5}=1^{5}=1\).

Step 4: Result
\[(1+\omega-\omega^{2})^{8}=256\,\omega\]
Why: Put Step 3 into Step 2.

Check: reach the power 8 by repeated squaring
\[(-2\omega^{2})^{2}=4\omega^{4}=4\omega\]
\[(4\omega)^{2}=16\omega^{2}\]
\[(16\omega^{2})^{2}=256\omega^{4}\]
\[=256\,\omega\]
Why: Squaring three times gives the 8th power (\(2\times2\times2=8\)); the same answer comes out.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The book prints \((1+\omega-\omega)^{8}\). Taken literally this is \(1^{8}=1\). The answer key's \(256\omega\) shows that the intended bracket is \((1+\omega-\omega^{2})\): the square on the last \(\omega\) is missing in print. We solved \((1+\omega-\omega^{2})^{8}=256\omega\).

blocks.explanation: An evaluation with \(\omega\): we must reduce the expression to a simple number using only \(\omega^{3}=1\) and \(1+\omega+\omega^{2}=0\). Plan: first turn each bracket into a single term (or recognise it as \(\omega\) or \(\omega^{2}\)), then raise to the power, then reduce the powers of \(\omega\) by dividing by 3.
steps:
Step 1: Reduce the two big powers
\[\omega^{28}=(\omega^{3})^{9}\cdot\omega=\omega\]
\[\omega^{29}=(\omega^{3})^{9}\cdot\omega^{2}=\omega^{2}\]
Why: \(28=27+1\) and \(29=27+2\); \(\omega^{27}=(\omega^{3})^{9}=1\), so only the remainders 1 and 2 matter.

Step 2: Use the main property
\[\omega^{28}+\omega^{29}+1=\omega+\omega^{2}+1\]
\[=0\]
Why: After reducing, the expression is exactly \(1+\omega+\omega^{2}\), which is 0.

Check: use the actual values
\[\omega+\omega^{2}=\dfrac{-1+\sqrt{3}i}{2}+\dfrac{-1-\sqrt{3}i}{2}\]
\[\omega+\omega^{2}=-1\]
\[-1+1=0\]
Why: The imaginary parts cancel and the real parts give \(-1\).

blocks.explanation: An evaluation with \(\omega\): we must reduce the expression to a simple number using only \(\omega^{3}=1\) and \(1+\omega+\omega^{2}=0\). Plan: first turn each bracket into a single term (or recognise it as \(\omega\) or \(\omega^{2}\)), then raise to the power, then reduce the powers of \(\omega\) by dividing by 3.
steps:
Step 1: Simplify the first bracket
\[1+\omega-\omega^{2}=(1+\omega)-\omega^{2}\]
\[=-\omega^{2}-\omega^{2}=-2\omega^{2}\]
Why: \(1+\omega=-\omega^{2}\), as in part (i).

Step 2: Simplify the second bracket
\[1-\omega+\omega^{2}=(1+\omega^{2})-\omega\]
\[=-\omega-\omega=-2\omega\]
Why: Here group 1 with \(\omega^{2}\): \(1+\omega^{2}=-\omega\).

Step 3: Multiply
\[(-2\omega^{2})(-2\omega)=4\omega^{3}\]
\[=4\]
Why: Minus times minus is plus, \(2\times2=4\), and \(\omega^{2}\cdot\omega=\omega^{3}=1\).

Check: a second route, (1 + A)(1 - A)
\[A=\omega-\omega^{2}\]
\[(1+A)(1-A)=1-A^{2}\]
\[A^{2}=\omega^{2}-2\omega^{3}+\omega^{4}\]
\[A^{2}=\omega^{2}-2+\omega=-3\]
\[1-A^{2}=1+3=4\]
Why: The two brackets are \(1+A\) and \(1-A\); using \(\omega^{4}=\omega\) and \(\omega+\omega^{2}=-1\) gives the same 4.

blocks.prompt: 2 (iv) Evaluate \(\left(\frac{-1+\sqrt{-3}}{2}\right)^{7}+\left(\frac{-1-\sqrt{-3}}{2}\right)^{7}\). [The book prints the first bracket as \(\frac{1+\sqrt{-3}}{2}\); see the book correction below.]
blocks.explanation: An evaluation with \(\omega\): we must reduce the expression to a simple number using only \(\omega^{3}=1\) and \(1+\omega+\omega^{2}=0\). Plan: first turn each bracket into a single term (or recognise it as \(\omega\) or \(\omega^{2}\)), then raise to the power, then reduce the powers of \(\omega\) by dividing by 3. Here the brackets are \(\omega\) and \(\omega^{2}\) in disguise.
steps:
Step 1: Recognise the brackets
\[\sqrt{-3}=\sqrt{3}\,i\]
\[\dfrac{-1+\sqrt{-3}}{2}=\omega\]
\[\dfrac{-1-\sqrt{-3}}{2}=\omega^{2}\]
Why: With \(\sqrt{-3}=\sqrt{3}i\) the brackets match the values of \(\omega\) and \(\omega^{2}\) exactly.

Step 2: Rewrite and reduce the powers
\[\omega^{7}+(\omega^{2})^{7}=\omega^{7}+\omega^{14}\]
\[\omega^{7}=(\omega^{3})^{2}\omega=\omega\]
\[\omega^{14}=(\omega^{3})^{4}\omega^{2}=\omega^{2}\]
Why: Power of a power multiplies the indices; \(7=6+1\) and \(14=12+2\).

Step 3: Add
\[\omega+\omega^{2}=-1\]
Why: From \(1+\omega+\omega^{2}=0\).

Step 4: What the printed expression gives
\[\dfrac{1+\sqrt{-3}}{2}=-\omega^{2}\]
\[(-\omega^{2})^{7}+(\omega^{2})^{7}\]
\[=-\omega^{14}+\omega^{14}=0\]
Why: Taking a minus sign out of \(\frac{1+\sqrt{3}i}{2}\) gives \(-\omega^{2}\); an odd power keeps the minus, so the two terms cancel. This is why the key's \(-1\) needs the first bracket \(\frac{-1+\sqrt{-3}}{2}\).

Check: conjugates
\[\omega^{14}=\omega^{2}=\overline{\omega}\]
\[\omega+\overline{\omega}=2\operatorname{Re}(\omega)\]
\[=2\left(-\tfrac{1}{2}\right)=-1\]
Why: A number plus its conjugate is twice its real part; the same \(-1\) comes out.
blocks.final_answer: \(-1\) (the expression exactly as printed, with \(\frac{1+\sqrt{-3}}{2}\), equals \(0\))

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The book prints the first bracket as \(\frac{1+\sqrt{-3}}{2}\), which is \(-\omega^{2}\); with it the sum is \(-\omega^{14}+\omega^{14}=0\). The answer key's \(-1\) is the value of \(\left(\frac{-1+\sqrt{-3}}{2}\right)^{7}+\left(\frac{-1-\sqrt{-3}}{2}\right)^{7}\), so a minus sign is missing before the 1. We solved the intended expression.

blocks.prompt: 2 (v) Evaluate \((-1+\sqrt{-3})^{5}+(-1-\sqrt{-3})^{5}\). [The book prints the first bracket as \((1+\sqrt{-3})\); see the book correction below.]
blocks.explanation: An evaluation with \(\omega\): we must reduce the expression to a simple number using only \(\omega^{3}=1\) and \(1+\omega+\omega^{2}=0\). Plan: first turn each bracket into a single term (or recognise it as \(\omega\) or \(\omega^{2}\)), then raise to the power, then reduce the powers of \(\omega\) by dividing by 3. This is like part (iv), but without the division by 2, so the brackets are \(2\omega\) and \(2\omega^{2}\).
steps:
Step 1: Write each bracket with omega
\[-1+\sqrt{-3}=-1+\sqrt{3}i=2\omega\]
\[-1-\sqrt{-3}=-1-\sqrt{3}i=2\omega^{2}\]
Why: \(-1+\sqrt{3}i=2\cdot\frac{-1+\sqrt{3}i}{2}=2\omega\); the same for the other bracket.

Step 2: Raise to the power 5
\[(2\omega)^{5}+(2\omega^{2})^{5}\]
\[=32\omega^{5}+32\omega^{10}\]
\[=32(\omega^{5}+\omega^{10})\]
Why: \(2^{5}=32\) and \((\omega^{2})^{5}=\omega^{10}\); then take 32 common.

Step 3: Reduce the powers and add
\[\omega^{5}=\omega^{3}\omega^{2}=\omega^{2}\]
\[\omega^{10}=(\omega^{3})^{3}\omega=\omega\]
\[32(\omega^{2}+\omega)=32(-1)\]
\[=-32\]
Why: \(5=3+2\), \(10=9+1\), and \(\omega+\omega^{2}=-1\).

Step 4: What the printed expression gives
\[1+\sqrt{-3}=-2\omega^{2}\]
\[(-2\omega^{2})^{5}+(2\omega^{2})^{5}=0\]
Why: \(1+\sqrt{3}i=-(-1-\sqrt{3}i)=-2\omega^{2}\); an odd power keeps the minus, so the two terms cancel. The key's \(-32\) needs \((-1+\sqrt{-3})\).

Check: conjugates
\[(2\omega)^{5}=32\omega^{2}\]
\[(2\omega^{2})^{5}=32\omega=\overline{32\omega^{2}}\]
\[\text{sum}=2\operatorname{Re}(32\omega^{2})\]
\[=64\left(-\tfrac{1}{2}\right)=-32\]
Why: The two terms are conjugates, so their sum is twice the real part.
blocks.final_answer: \(-32\) (the expression exactly as printed, with \((1+\sqrt{-3})\), equals \(0\))

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The book prints the first bracket as \((1+\sqrt{-3})\), which is \(-2\omega^{2}\); with it the sum is \((-2\omega^{2})^{5}+(2\omega^{2})^{5}=0\). The answer key's \(-32\) is the value of \((-1+\sqrt{-3})^{5}+(-1-\sqrt{-3})^{5}\), so a minus sign is missing before the 1. We solved the intended expression.
